To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there is a significant difference between the importance attributed to the factors that affect the implementation of quality management programs, according to the size of the firm.

(1) the most important factors that hinder quality programs’ implementation are top management education and training, costs and actual performances and aversion to change; (2) the most important factor that hinders quality programs’ implementation in medium-sized firms is aversion to change.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (a) to identify/analyze factors that hinder the implementation of quality improvement programs in Portuguese SMEs, and (b) to test if the importance attributed to these factors differs according to the firm's dimension.

the following issues: first, the main factors that affect quality programs’ implementation in Portuguese SMEs; and second, the differences in importance attributed to those barriers, according to firms’ dimensions.
the factors hindering the implementation of quality improvement programs in SME.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the factors that hinder quality programs’ implementation are: top management's level of education and training, top management's priorities, costs and current performance, lack of external support, overload of human resources, aversion to changes, lack of resources and culture and training.

the main factors that hamper quality improvement programs in SMEs are related to: top management's priorities, lack of resources and support, aversion to innovation, and lack of human resources' training.

the quality programs implementation in Portuguese SME is hindered by the following factors: top management's priorities, costs and performance, lack of external support, human resources’ load, aversion to changes, lack of resources and culture and training.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the paper identifies a set of seven factors that affect quality improvement programs’ (QIP) implementation in SME.
the paper identifies a set of factors that hinder quality programs’ implementation in small firms, and that the importance attributed to these factors differ according to SMEs’ dimension.

the main factors hindering the implementation of quality programs in SME are: top management's lack of training/education and priorities, lack of support of external agents, costs and actual results, lack of human resources, aversion to changes, lack of resources and culture and training.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quality of a firm’s products is a key driver of firm value.
the quality of the implementation of a program can have a greater impact on its success than the quality of its design.
the quality of the data is a critical factor in achieving the desired results.
